task: Achieve coordinated multimodal assembly and locomotion of modular magnetic cubes under global magnetic field control
key_results: Demonstrated parallel 2D assembly, pivot walking with half-structure-length per-cycle displacement, rolling locomotion at ~3 body lengths/cycle, and vertical stacking via tilted pivot walking; all controlled via single global Helmholtz coil without agent-specific inputs
comments: The multiplex workspace exploiting boundary-mediated symmetry breaking is clever and scalable, though coordination complexity may increase significantly with larger cube numbers.

model_io.model: Magnetic modular cubes (2 mm edge, 10 Nd micro-magnets, face-specific encoding)
inputs: global uniform magnetic field (triaxial Helmholtz coil)

model_io.model: Dipole interaction model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Boundary-mediated symmetry breaking enables differentiated manipulation of multiple module groups without local sensing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by parallel 2D assembly and selective locomotion modes achieved via global field modulation
